decision: Treat corrupt or unreadable owner metadata as fail-closed; reserve age-based orphan recovery only for an ownerless lock directory where owner.json is genuinely absent.
problem: The lock recovery path previously caught JSON parse/read failures and could reclaim the lock based only on directory age. A corrupt owner.json could therefore be treated as an orphan after the grace period even when a live writer still owned the lock.

reviews.correctness: Preferred distinguishing owner.json absence from malformed/unreadable metadata. Absence can occur in the short mkdir-to-owner-publish window; corrupt metadata cannot safely prove ownership or death.
reviews.robustness_security: Preferred fail-closed behavior for parse errors and non-ENOENT read failures so damaged metadata cannot become an ownership bypass. Existing PID liveness plus process-start identity remains the authority when valid metadata exists.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Preferred a control-flow fix in the existing filesystem lock over a database, lock daemon, or extra probes. It adds no network/Qubes round trips and negligible local overhead.

alternatives_rejected: Reclaim any unreadable owner after orphanGraceMs: can steal a live writer lock when metadata is corrupted or temporarily inaccessible.
Never use age-based recovery: leaves a crash between mkdir(lockPath) and publishing owner.json unrecoverable.
Move immediately to a database/lock daemon: larger operational and regression surface than required for the same-host Slice 1 contract.
qa: Malformed structured owner metadata fails closed.
Corrupt JSON fails closed even when the lock directory is older than orphanGraceMs.
Live owner with unverifiable process identity is not stolen.
Dead owner with valid metadata and unavailable identity remains reclaimable via independent liveness.
A genuinely ownerless lock directory remains eligible for bounded age-based recovery.
failure_lessons: A catch-all recovery branch can silently turn metadata corruption into an ownership bypass.
Orphan recovery must distinguish missing publication from untrusted/corrupt publication.
Fail-closed metadata handling is more important than aggressive stale-lock recovery before Qubes/process-per-call transport is layered on top.
remaining_risks: The filesystem lock remains same-host only, not a distributed lock across coordinator machines.
Ownerless-directory recovery still depends on mtime/orphanGraceMs and should be exercised across real OS process crashes.
Hosted CI execution remains an independent blocker for executable proof of this Slice.
